posts.text: The fact that California elections often can't be resolved for weeks is kind of insane and not common in other electoral systems around the world.
Like honestly "it's going to take us several weeks to tell you who won the election" is failed state shit and should be much more stigmatized.
The fact that it's tolerated is bad too a textbook example of learned helplessness.

Yeah, it's pretty bad. Saying "this doesn't matter, Graham is focused on the issues," etc. is fine and sort of on-brand, but the threats against the former staffer are very dubious and also very establishment-y and "political" for that matter.


Brien Jackson (@Brien_Jackson)

It's worth pointing out that, contra the Platner degenerates, it is absolutely not normal campaign behavior to threaten a former staffer if they refuse to go on the record with an outright lie to major media organizations.

Whether there's something more there or not (maybe not), there's a little bit of Biden post-debate in the @katz_morris strategy, i.e., let's try to gut this through until the withdrawal deadline passes in mid-July and Dems *literally* have no choice.

Look I don't really GAF who's sexting who. But why are Platner campaign advisors like @katz_morris  threatening ex-staffers as if they disclosed nuclear secrets? Because in a democracy, it's the people's job to decide what matters, and they know it might be damaging.


austerity is theft (@wideofthepost)

There is no “sexting scandal.” There’s nothing scandalous here. The Platners resolved this before they decided to run for senate and brought this up on their own campaign self-vetting — which t

The whole narrative they built is Platner had youthful, drunken indiscretions and was on a redemption arc. Which was always probably bullshit, and this story speaks to that. Voters can/should vote for him anyway if they share his policy goals! But that's up for them to decide.

BTW you're also gambling on something much worse not coming out after the withdrawal deadline passes in mid-July, which I don't think anyone in this argument is so dishonest as to not be concerned about.
There's been lots of people pointing to the polls to allay concerns about Platner. But polls have underestimated Republicans by an average of 4 points in Maine since 2014.

That's from today's (free) newsletter about the state of play in Maine. Lots more here:
natesilver.net/p/should-demo…

Our World Cup projections are set to publish this week! We’re hoping within 48 hours, assuming final testing goes well. 🤞

In the meantime, here are our updated PELE ratings, accounting for recent friendly matches, including USA’s 2-1 win over Senegal yesterday.

The USA is up to #28, reflecting some recent progress, but is considerably lower than where FIFA has them (#16). However, home-field advantage is quite large in International soccer and should help USA/CAN/MEX. More to come soon, but here's the PELE page.
natesilver.net/p/pele-intern…

Ok but if someone is charming in person and then you find out they're a manipulative narcissist it becomes extremely hard to trust that initial interaction. In fact you might often feel betrayed.


Ryan Grim (@ryangrim)

I think this would be true if Platner was running to represent a state with tens of millions of people. But he needs to win the votes of just several hundred thousand to win and he will have spoken face to face with possibly a majority of them by the time this campaign is over.

The ex-staffers speaking out against Platner is a very bad signal too. Democratic staffers are mostly risk-averse types who want to preserve their equity for future jobs, not the types to get out of line if they think their candidate is a good person at heart.

Idk I guess Platner is still the favorite but there's a tipping point between "this guy is a little rough around the edges" (and maybe that makes him "authentic" scare quotes extremely necessary there) vs. "this guy is just a toxic dude".
Also the "authenticity" reads as super performative when you're an obvious narcissist.
